author: Rahul kp
topic: Exempt vs Nil-rated vs Zero-rated Supply
title: Exempt vs Zero-rated
simple_words: Exempt, nil-rated and non-taxable supplies lose ITC. Zero-rated supply (export, SEZ) keeps ITC and can get a refund.

definitions.meaning: Supply on which no tax is payable. It includes nil-rated supply, wholly exempt supply and non-taxable supply.
definitions.note: Inputs used for it get no ITC

definitions.meaning: Export of goods or services, or supply to an SEZ developer or SEZ unit for authorised operations (IGST Act).

key_points: Nil-rated, wholly exempt and non-taxable supplies all fall under ==exempt supply== for ITC purposes
ITC used ==exclusively== for exempt supplies is not available at all
!!ITC on common inputs is reversed in proportion!! to exempt supplies (Sec 17(2) and 17(3), CGST Act)
==Zero-rated== supply is a separate category: ITC stays and refund can be claimed
formula_hook: spot the type, spot the ITC

rows: Tax relief by notification or law
Outside GST, e.g. alcohol for human use

insight.punchline: Exempt loses ITC, zero-rated keeps it!
insight.text: Zero-rated supply keeps ITC and refund even if the same goods are otherwise exempt when sold locally.

memory_trick.mnemonic: Zero Zooms out, Exempt Eats ITC
memory_trick.explanation: Zero-rated goods zoom out of India or into SEZ and come back with a refund. Exempt supply stays home and eats (loses) the ITC.

steps: If no: is any tax payable?
exam_tip: In MCQs, first check for export or SEZ. Zero-rated supply is a separate category: ITC and refund are allowed even if the goods are otherwise exempt.

doubt.question: Is nil-rated supply the same as zero-rated supply?
doubt.answer: No. Nil-rated is a domestic supply at 0% rate and counts as exempt, so ITC is lost. Zero-rated is export or SEZ supply and keeps ITC.

mistakes.wrong: Treating nil-rated supply as zero-rated and allowing ITC
mistakes.right: Nil-rated is an exempt supply. ITC is not available on inputs used exclusively for it.

mistakes.wrong: Saying all ITC is blocked if a business makes some exempt supplies
mistakes.right: Only exclusive-use ITC is blocked; ITC on common inputs is reversed in proportion (Sec 17(2), 17(3), CGST Act).

mistakes.wrong: Treating every supply to an SEZ as zero-rated
mistakes.right: Zero-rated only if made to an SEZ developer or unit for authorised operations.

mistakes.wrong: Denying ITC on exports because the goods are exempt
mistakes.right: Export is zero-rated; ITC is allowed even if the supply is otherwise exempt.

Checker 1: Definition 1 meaning and Steps 3–4 ('no tax is payable' / 'If no: is any tax payable? None payable: exempt'): 'no tax payable' is looser than Sec 2(47). A supply taxed under reverse charge also has no tax payable by the supplier, but it is not an exempt supply. Better: 'Supply attracting a nil rate of tax, wholly exempt under Sec 11 CGST / Sec 6 IGST, or a non-taxable supply (Sec 2(47), CGST Act)'. Step 3 better: 'If no: is it nil-rated, wholly exempt or non-taxable?'

Checker 1: Key point 3 / Mistake 2 right: you could add that the proportionate reversal is worked out under Rules 42/43 of the CGST Rules, and that under the Explanation to Sec 17(3), Schedule III activities other than sale of land, and of buildings after the completion certificate (Sch II para 5(b)), are left out of the value of exempt supply. This adds precision; nothing in the note is wrong.
